reviews.text:
Buraya gönderilen çocuk akıllı ise, atheist olur. Akılsız ise bunlara asker/köle olur.

Bugün ki cuma vaazında imtihan edilmemiz için dua etmesi önerildi. Sabır istemenin yanlış olduğu anlatıldı ve imtihanların üstesinden sadece peygamberlerin gelebildiği söylendi. Bu başlı başına yanlıştır. Cennet bedava değildir ve her birimiz imtihanlardan geçeceğiz. Burası bir imtihan dünyasıdır. Imtihan edilmemek akla, mantığa uymaz. Kuranda bakara suresi 214. Ayetde boşuna "Sizden önce gelenlerin durumu sizin başıniza gelmeden cennete gireceğinizi mi zannettiniz? Peygamber ve onunla beraber müminler: "Allahin yardımı ne zaman?" diyecek kadar darlıiğa ve zorluğa uğramışlar ve sarsilmişlardı; iyi bilin ki Allahin yardımı şüphesiz yakındır." Denmiyor

Ayrıca Hz. İbrahimin oğlunu kurban etmesi ele alındı. Hz. Ibrahimin bir rüya sonucu oğlunu kurban etmeye çalışması ve oğlunun İttihat etmesinin takdir edilmesi gerektiği söylendi. Şimdi ki çocuklar böyle İttihat etmeyecekleri eleştirildi. Hz. İbrahimin bir peygamber olarak Allah'tan gelen bir emir olduğu arka planda kaldı. Vahiy belki rüya yolu ile gelmiş olabilir, ama asıl önemli olan allahtan gelen bir vahiy olmasıdır. Şimdi ki zamanda bir baba ben rüyamda gördüm oğlumu kesecem dese tabikide evladı buna karşı çıkacak. Hangimiz peygamberiz de Allahtan böyle bir vahiy alacağız. Sanki islam dininde saçma sapan görülen rüyalara göre hareket ediliyor. Bir insan rüyasında alkol tüketip zina işlese, bu Allah'ın emri mi olacak? Bu aptallıktır! Akıllı hic bir insanı böylece islama inandıramazsınız, ısındıramazsınız. Mantığa aykırı olmasına rağmen İttihat etmeye yönlendirilmiş bir vaaz.

Bu yüzden buraya eğitime gönderilen bir çocuk bu yüzden ya atheist olarak çıkar veyahut bunların askeri/kölesi olarak çıkar.
reviews.textTranslated:
If a child sent here is intelligent, he becomes an atheist. If he is unintelligent, he becomes a soldier/slave to them.

In today's Friday sermon, it was suggested that we pray for being tested. It was explained that asking for patience is wrong, and that only prophets can overcome trials. This is fundamentally wrong. Paradise is not free, and each of us will go through trials. This is a world of trials. Not being tested is illogical and unreasonable. The 214th verse of the Surah Al-Baqarah in the Quran is not without reason: "Do you think that you will enter Paradise without being afflicted with what those before you were afflicted with, and the Messenger and those with him were afflicted with hardship and distress, and they cried out, 'When will the help of Allah come?' Indeed, the help of Allah is near."

Furthermore, the story of Prophet Abraham sacrificing his son was discussed. It was said that Prophet Abraham's attempt to sacrifice his son as a result of a dream, and his son's acceptance of the situation, should be appreciated. The criticism was that today's children wouldn't unite in this way. The fact that Abraham was a prophet and received a divine command was overlooked. Revelation might have come through dreams, but the crucial point is that it was a divine revelation. Nowadays, if a father says in a dream, "I saw in a dream I'm going to kill my son," his son will naturally object. Which of us is a prophet to receive such a revelation from God? It's as if Islam is based on absurd dreams. If a person consumes alcohol and commits adultery in a dream, would that be a command from God? That's foolish! You can't convince or warm up to Islam in this way for any intelligent person. It's a sermon aimed at uniting, despite being illogical.

Therefore, a child sent here for education will either emerge as an atheist or as a soldier/slave of these groups.

Müslümanlık İnceliktir, Kimseyi Mahcup Etmek Değildir!Dostlar,

bir gencin camiye gelirken arkadaşlarıyla camiye Alisan gençlerin o sessiz mahcubiyeti hiç düşündünüz mü? İbadete yeni heves etmiş, kalbi huzur arayan bir gençlerimiz , her Cuma namazı safların arasından geçen o kutuyu gördüğünde başını öne eğmek zorunda kalıyorsa burada durup bir düşünmemiz gerekir.
İman sadece namaz kılmak değil, mümin kardeşinin halinden anlamak, onun onurunu korumaktır. "Cebimde para yok, mahcup olurum" diyerek camiden ayağını çeken bir gencin vebali, o kutuyu safların arasında gezdirenlerin omzundadır. Müslümanlık dilencilik değil, gönül rızasıyla gizlice infak etmektir.

Cikisa bir kutu konulur gönlü olan kalkar parasını atar .Hayat zorlaştı eskisi gibi değil lütfen insanları mahcup duruma sokmayin.Gönülleri Asilolan Gönül Almaktır: "Güzel bir söz bağışlama, peşinden gönül kırma gelen bir sadakadan daha hayırlıdır." (Bakara Suresi, 263) Allah, kırılan bir kalbin üzerine inşa edilen yardımı reddediyor!
Dilenerek yardım toplanilmaz.Ben bunu bütün camiler için söylüyorum.Buna derhal son verilsin Insanlari camiden soğutmayın .

Peygamber Efendimiz (s.a.v.) buyuruyor ki: "Müjdeleyiniz, nefret ettirmeyiniz; kolaylaştırınız, zorlaştırmayınız. Gelin, bu yanlışa hep birlikte 'dur' diyelim ki; camilerimiz mahcubiyetin değil, huzurun merkezi kalsın.
reviews.textTranslated:
Islam is about refinement, not about humiliating anyone! Friends,

Have you ever considered the silent shyness of young people coming to the mosque with their friends? If our young people, newly eager for worship and seeking peace in their hearts, are forced to lower their heads when they see that box passing between the rows every Friday prayer, we need to stop and think. Faith is not just about praying; it's about understanding the plight of your fellow believer and protecting their dignity. The responsibility for a young person who avoids the mosque saying, "I don't have any money, I'll be embarrassed," lies on the shoulders of those who carry that box between the rows. Islam is not about begging, but about giving secretly and willingly.

A box is placed at the exit, and those with a heart can get up and put in their money. Life has become difficult; it's not like it used to be. Please don't put people in embarrassing situations. The noblest thing is to win hearts: "A kind word of forgiveness is better than charity followed by hurting someone's feelings." (Surah Al-Baqarah, 263) Allah rejects charity built upon a broken heart! Charity cannot be collected by begging. I say this for all mosques. This must end immediately. Do not alienate people from the mosque.

Our Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Give glad tidings, do not cause aversion; make things easy, do not make them difficult." Let us all together say 'stop' to this wrong so that our mosques remain centers of peace, not shame.

reviews.name: Basaran Aydin
reviews.text:
Ein Ort des Friedens, der Gemeinschaft und der Inspiration!

Die Moschee in Duisburg-Homberg (VIKZ) ist ein absoluter Schatz für unsere Gemeinde! Schon beim Betreten spürt man die warme, einladende Atmosphäre – sauber, hell und mit wunderschöner Architektur, die Ruhe und Spiritualität ausstrahlt. Die Gebetsräume sind geräumig, die Böden weich und einladend, und die Kalligrafie an den Wänden berührt das Herz.

**Was mich besonders begeistert:**
- **Gemeinschaft & Integration**: Hier trifft man Menschen aller Altersgruppen und Hintergründe.  Es fühlt sich nicht wie Rückzug an, sondern wie Brücke zur Gesellschaft!
- **Offene Türen**: Regelmäßige Moscheeführungen und der "Tag der offenen Moschee" machen es zu einem Ort des Dialogs. Christen, Nicht-Muslime – alle sind willkommen, Vorurteile werden abgebaut.
- **Religiöse Qualität**: Die Imame predigen moderat, integrationsfördernd und auf Deutsch. Die Jugendkurse sind super strukturiert und verbinden Glauben mit Bildung.
- **Service**: Freundliches Personal, saubere Einrichtungen, sogar Parkplätze in der Nähe. Alles top organisiert!

Diese Moschee stärkt nicht nur den Glauben, sondern unsere gesamte Nachbarschaft. Ein echtes Vorbild für Toleranz und Zusammenhalt in Deutschland. Ich komme wöchentlich her und empfehle sie jedem – ob Gläubiger oder Neugieriger. Danke, VIKZ-Team, für diesen wunderbaren Ort! 🙏🕌
reviews.textTranslated:
A place of peace, community, and inspiration!

The mosque in Duisburg-Homberg (VIKZ) is an absolute treasure for our community! The moment you step inside, you feel the warm, welcoming atmosphere – clean, bright, and with beautiful architecture that radiates tranquility and spirituality. The prayer rooms are spacious, the floors soft and inviting, and the calligraphy on the walls touches the heart.

**What I find particularly inspiring:**

- **Community & Integration**: Here you meet people of all ages and backgrounds. It doesn't feel like a place of retreat, but rather a bridge to society!

- **Open Doors**: Regular mosque tours and the "Open Mosque Day" make it a place of dialogue. Christians, non-Muslims – everyone is welcome, and prejudices are broken down.

- **Religious Quality**: The imams preach in a moderate, integration-oriented manner and in German. The youth courses are exceptionally well-structured and combine faith with education.

**Service**: Friendly staff, clean facilities, and even parking nearby. Everything is perfectly organized!

This mosque not only strengthens faith but also our entire neighborhood. A true example of tolerance and community spirit in Germany. I come here weekly and recommend it to everyone – whether a believer or simply curious. Thank you, VIKZ team, for this wonderful place! 🙏🕌

reviews.name: Sonnenschein Moonlight
reviews.text:
Wenn ich weniger als einen Stern vergeben könnte, würde ich keinen Moment zögern. Was ich heute erlebt habe, war bis ins Äußerste widerlich und beschämend.

Früher gab es dort ein Iftar speziell für Frauen, und auch im letzten Ramadan war das so. Deshalb bin ich heute nach meiner Arbeit, die sich in der Nähe befindet, dorthin gegangen, um mein Fasten zu brechen. Ich wusste nicht, dass es kein Iftar mehr für Frauen gibt. Da keine Frauen anwesend waren, brachte mir mein Mann Essen aus dem Männerbereich, und ich setzte mich in den Raum, der früher für Frauen vorgesehen war, und aß ruhig.

Nach kurzer Zeit kam ein Mitarbeiter und setzte sich ebenfalls dort hin, um zu essen. Es lag mir fern, jemanden wegzuschicken. Dann erschien ein älterer Mann, der mich ohne jede Erklärung oder Vorwarnung auf äußerst grobe und respektlose Weise ansprach. Er schrie mich an: „Raus! Raus!“, in einem herablassenden und demütigenden Ton, ohne auch nur im Ansatz zu erklären, was das Problem sei.

Später erklärte mir ein syrischer Mann, dass es kein Iftar mehr speziell für Frauen gibt. Doch derjenige, der mich hinauswarf, hielt es nicht einmal für nötig, mir das ruhig zu erklären. Stattdessen zeigte er ein Maß an Härte und Respektlosigkeit, das weder menschlich noch akzeptabel ist – schon gar nicht für jemanden, der einen öffentlichen Ort repräsentiert.

Ich stellte mich zur Seite und wartete auf meinen Mann, damit wir gehen konnten. Trotzdem versuchte er erneut, mich zu vertreiben, mit der Begründung, auf der gegenüberliegenden Seite säßen Männer. Immer wieder wiederholte er aggressiv das Wort „haram“, als hätte ich ein schweres Vergehen begangen – dabei saß ich lediglich in einem geschlossenen Raum und aß, ohne irgendjemandem zu schaden.

Würde der Prophet (Friede und Segen seien auf ihm) mit solcher Grobheit, Härte und Respektlosigkeit gegenüber einer Frau umgehen, die in einem Raum sitzt und ihr Fasten bricht?
Vielmehr hätte er zu dem anderen Mann gesagt: „Geh und iss mit den Männern und lass die Frau in Ruhe ihr Fasten brechen.“ Danach hätte er ihr freundlich und respektvoll erklärt, dass es kein Iftar mehr speziell für Frauen gibt.
Das sind die wahren Werte und die Moral des Islam – nicht ein Verhalten wie das, das ich heute bei euch erlebt habe. Wenn sich Regeln geändert haben, hätte ein freundliches Wort und eine respektvolle Erklärung vollkommen ausgereicht. Charakter zeigt sich in schwierigen Momenten – und was ich heute erlebt habe, hatte nichts mit Anstand oder Respekt zu tun.

Denn im Islam heißt es: „Die Religion ist gutes Verhalten (ad-dīn al-muʿāmalah). Das bedeutet, dass sich wahrer Glaube im Umgang mit den Menschen zeigt – in Respekt, Barmherzigkeit und Anstand. Was ich heute erlebt habe, steht im klaren Widerspruch zu diesen Werten.

Dieser Mann sollte sich schämen und neu lernen, was Respekt, Menschlichkeit und die wahren Werte des Islam bedeuten. Was heute geschehen ist, hat mich zutiefst verletzt. Noch nie in meinem Leben wurde ich so grob und herablassend behandelt.
reviews.textTranslated:
If I could give less than one star, I wouldn't hesitate for a moment. What I experienced today was utterly disgusting and shameful.

There used to be a separate Iftar for women there, and it was the same last Ramadan. That's why I went there today after work, which is nearby, to break my fast. I didn't know that there was no longer an Iftar for women. Since there were no women present, my husband brought me food from the men's section, and I sat down in the room that used to be reserved for women and ate quietly.

After a short time, a staff member came and sat down there to eat as well. I had no intention of sending anyone away. Then an older man appeared and, without any explanation or warning, addressed me in an extremely rude and disrespectful manner. He shouted at me, "Get out! Get out!" in a condescending and humiliating tone, without even attempting to explain what the problem was.


After a short while, a staff member came and sat down to eat as well. Later, a Syrian man explained to me that there is no longer a separate Iftar for women. However, the man who threw me out didn't even bother to explain this calmly. Instead, he displayed a level of harshness and disrespect that is neither humane nor acceptable—especially for someone representing a public space.

I stepped aside and waited for my husband so we could leave. Even so, he tried again to expel me, claiming there were men sitting on the opposite side. He aggressively repeated the word "haram" as if I had committed some grave offense—when all I was doing was sitting in an enclosed space eating without harming anyone.

Would the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) have treated a woman in such rudeness, harshness, and disrespect while she was sitting in a room breaking her fast?

Rather, he would have said to the other man, "Go and eat with the men and let the woman break her fast in peace." He should have then kindly and respectfully explained to her that there is no longer a separate Iftar meal for women.

These are the true values ​​and morals of Islam—not the kind of behavior I witnessed today. If the rules have changed, a kind word and a respectful explanation would have been perfectly sufficient. Character is revealed in difficult moments—and what I experienced today had nothing to do with decency or respect.

For Islam states: “Religion is good conduct (ad-dīn al-muʿāmalah).” This means that true faith is demonstrated in how we treat others—in respect, compassion, and decency. What I experienced today is in clear contradiction to these values.

This man should be ashamed and relearn what respect, humanity, and the true values ​​of Islam mean. What happened today has deeply hurt me. Never in my life have I been treated so rudely and condescendingly.

reviews.text:
Sehr sehr schöner Ort, kann ich nur empfehlen :)
Natürlich kann jeder freiwillig spenden, aber es gibt zwei Arten von Spende: 1. Teberru ; 2. Sadaka. Beide sind schöne Taten, aber es gibt feine Unterschiede:
Teberru
Ein weitgefasster Begriff — umfasst jede Art freiwilliger Schenkung
Religiöse Absicht ist nicht zwingend — auch für weltliche Zwecke möglich (Blutspende, Eigentumsübertragung an eine Stiftung usw.)
Hat eine rechtliche und institutionelle Dimension (Stiftungsrecht, Medizinethik usw.)
Empfänger kann eine Person, eine Institution oder die Gesellschaft sein
In die Moschee gehen und Sadaka geben
Eine konkretere Handlung — ein bestimmter Ort, eine bestimmte Absicht
Klar religiös motiviert — wird getan, um Verdienst (Sevap) zu erlangen
Empfänger ist in der Regel ein Armer oder Bedürftiger
Unterscheidet sich von der Zakat (einer der fünf Säulen des Islam) — Sadaka ist freiwillig und hat keinen festgelegten Betrag
Kurz gesagt
Jede Sadaka ist ein Teberru, aber nicht jedes Teberru ist eine Sadaka.
In die Moschee zu gehen und Sadaka zu geben ist eine religiöse und praktische Unterform des Teberru. Teberru hingegen ist der übergeordnete Begriff, der sowohl religiöse als auch weltliche freiwillige Schenkungen umfasst. Letztendlich wird keiner überrumpelt oder sonst irgendwas gemacht, sondern es wird (wie beschrieben) Teberru gemacht :)
reviews.textTranslated:
A very, very beautiful place, I highly recommend it :)
Of course, everyone is welcome to donate voluntarily, but there are two types of donation: 1. Teberru; 2. Sadaka. Both are noble acts, but there are subtle differences:
Teberru
A broad term—encompassing any kind of voluntary donation
Religious intent is not mandatory—also possible for secular purposes (blood donation, transferring property to a foundation, etc.)
Has a legal and institutional dimension (foundation law, medical ethics, etc.)
Recipient can be a person, an institution, or society
Going to the mosque and giving Sadaka
A more specific act—a particular place, a specific intention
Clearly religiously motivated—done to gain merit (Sevap)
Recipient is usually poor or needy
Different from Zakat (one of the five pillars of Islam)—Sadaka is voluntary and has no fixed amount
In short, every Sadaka is a Teberru, but not every Teberru is a Sadaka.
Going to the mosque and giving Sadaka is a religious and practical sub-form of Teberru. Teberru, on the other hand, is the overarching term that encompasses both religious and secular voluntary gifts. Ultimately, no one is pressured or anything like that; rather, Teberru is done (as described) :)

reviews.text: Ich war jetzt schon mehrmals in der Mehmet Akif Camii in Duisburg und bin jedes Mal wirklich positiv überrascht. Die Moschee ist sehr sauber und gepflegt, man merkt einfach, dass sich hier viele Menschen Mühe geben. Die Atmosphäre ist ruhig und angenehm, man kann dort gut abschalten und zur Ruhe kommen. Besonders schön finde ich das respektvolle Miteinander – egal ob jung oder alt, man wird freundlich begrüßt und fühlt sich direkt willkommen. Auch die Organisation wirkt durchdacht und strukturiert. Insgesamt ein sehr schöner Ort mit einer starken Gemeinschaft, den ich auf jeden Fall weiterempfehlen kann.
reviews.textTranslated: I've visited the Mehmet Akif Mosque in Duisburg several times now and am always pleasantly surprised. The mosque is very clean and well-maintained; you can tell that many people put a lot of effort into it. The atmosphere is calm and pleasant, a place to unwind and find peace. I especially appreciate the respectful interaction – regardless of age, everyone is greeted warmly and immediately feels welcome. The organization also seems well-planned and structured. Overall, it's a wonderful place with a strong community, and I would definitely recommend it.

Sie verfügt über einen Aufenthaltsraum, der als beliebtes Café gilt, insbesondere bei Jugendlichen und allen, die nach seelischer Ruhe suchen.
reviews.textTranslated: A beautiful mosque in the Turkish-Islamic style, where one can feel the religious and spiritual atmosphere, which conveys a sense of security and peace. After prayer, one feels as if the psychological pressures that burden the soul and mind have been released, and leaves the mosque with a feeling of relief and an uplifted spirit. It has a lounge that is a popular café, especially among young people and anyone seeking inner peace.

reviews.name: Sevgi Diribas
reviews.text: Marxloh daki Ulu Caminin her yıl ilkbahar da güzel yeşilliklerde yaptıkları Kermesi aslında çok beğeniyordum, 13 senedir bilirim, ama ne yazık ki bu sene çok hayal kırıklığına uratıldık ailecek. Yemekler nerdeyse hepsi soğuk verildi, mesela Mantı soğuk verilirmi? Yetmiyor muş gibi çok kötü kokuyordu bence bozulmuştu kıyması kokmuştu, yenisini aldım yeni kaynatılmış meğer aynıymış, ben sandım belki orda durdu diye öyle olmuş ama meğer hepsi öyle, ikinci bir kere geri gidip birdaha söylemedim çünkü inanmadılar bana. İçli köfte aldım buz gibi! Bir kere içli köfte kızarmış içi yağlı böyle soğuk yenmez ve bir ufacık parça Limon yok suni limon da yok biraz akıtacak daha lezzetli olması için zaten o da hiç iyi değildi. Lahmacün ler meğer camiide pişirilip oraya getirilyor tabii o da soğuyor ve özelliğini kaybediyor, neyseki hanım bayan bir Pan aletinde bize biraz ısıttı ama onuda sevemedik. Yanına çay aldık ama kızım hiç içemedi bile çünkü hepimiz tuhaf bir koku aldık, vardı çayda kokladık hiç iyi olmadı. Ya yani Kermesde Çay damı güzel olmaz artık? Daha yeni geldiğimizde bir ev yemeği kalmamıştı ne Sarma ne Dolma ve orda az kalmış Salatalar vardı biz fiş ile obir şeyleri alana kadar da saat 18:de bitti tüm değişik yemekler salatalar. Ee insan ancak o saatte gelebiliyor bazen işden sonra okuldan sonra yani 17-18 çok mu geç. Biz bu aldığımız kötü kokan yemeklerden sonra artık pasta tatlı da içimize sinmez derken zaten ne tatlı kalmıştı nede bir iyi pasta, börek de hiç yoktu fişi kaldı çaycı da üstünde daha 1 çay olan fişi aldı vermedi bir dikkat etmedim 1 dakika gitti yani. Eskiden hiç öyle değildi bu kermesde çok güzel yemekler ve candan çalışanlar vardı.. evet yine ellerinize emeğinize sağlık hepinizin uğraşıyorsunuz, ama yazmak istedim bilesiniz diye ve dahada çok kötüye gitmesin diye.
reviews.textTranslated: I've always really liked the annual spring fair held by the Grand Mosque in Marxloh, in its beautiful green surroundings – I've known about it for 13 years – but unfortunately, this year was a huge disappointment for my family. Almost all the food was served cold. For example, is it acceptable to serve mantı (Turkish dumplings) cold? And as if that wasn't enough, it smelled terrible; I think the minced meat was spoiled. I bought a new one, freshly boiled, but it turned out it was the same. I thought maybe it was just sitting there, but apparently they were all like that. I didn't go back and ask again because they didn't believe me. I got stuffed meatballs (İçli Köfte) and they were ice cold! First of all, stuffed meatballs are fried, greasy inside, and you can't eat them cold. And there wasn't even a tiny piece of lemon, or artificial lemon juice to make them more flavorful, which wasn't good at all. The lahmacun (Turkish pizza) was apparently cooked at the mosque and brought there, so it gets cold and loses its quality. Thankfully, a lady warmed them up a bit in a pan for us, but we didn't like that either. We bought tea, but my daughter couldn't even drink it because we all smelled a strange odor; we smelled the tea and it didn't taste good at all. I mean, is tea at a fair really not good anymore? When we arrived, there was no homemade food left – no stuffed grape leaves, no stuffed peppers, and only a few salads. By the time we got our receipts and other things, it was 6 PM and all the different dishes and salads were gone. Well, people can only get there around that time sometimes, after work or school, so 5 or 6 PM is too late. After those bad-smelling foods, we were thinking that even cakes and desserts wouldn't be good, but there weren't any desserts left, no good cakes or pastries at all. The tea vendor took the receipt, which still had one cup of tea on it, and didn't give it back. I didn't pay attention, it was just a minute away. It wasn't like this before; there used to be delicious food and friendly staff at this fair. Yes, thank you all for your hard work and effort, but I wanted to write this so you'd know and so things don't get any worse.

reviews.name: Muhamed Memis
reviews.text:
★★★★★ – Ein Ort, der mein Herz trägt
Die IGBD Duisburg e. V. ist für mich weit mehr als bloß eine Moschee; sie ist ein tief verwurzelter und prägender Teil meiner Lebensgeschichte. Hier durfte ich heranwachsen, meine ersten Gebete verrichten, den Glauben verinnerlichen, tiefgehende Gemeinschaft erfahren und stets Trost finden, wenn die Widrigkeiten des Lebens mich herausforderten.
Dieser Ort ist ein Refugium, an dem mein Herz zur Ruhe kommt. Schon beim Betreten umfängt einen eine besondere Aura: eine Stille, erfüllt von tiefem Frieden und innerer Einkehr. Eine Wärme, die von den Menschen, vom aufrichtig gelebten Glauben und der spürbaren Nähe zu Allah herrührt. Hier wird der Islam mit Liebe und Authentizität praktiziert – nicht oberflächlich oder prunkvoll, sondern tief aus dem Herzen und mit aufrichtiger Hingabe.
Was mich stets aufs Neue beeindruckt und tief berührt, ist die makellose Reinheit dieses Ortes. Die Sauberkeit der Moschee ist außergewöhnlich; alles ist bis ins kleinste Detail liebevoll gepflegt und zeugt von höchster Sorgfalt. Man spürt, dass dieser Ort zutiefst geehrt wird, nicht nur durch Worte, sondern durch jede Handlung, ganz im Einklang mit den erhabenen Lehren unseres Glaubens.
Und was wäre diese Moschee ohne die unermüdlichen Persönlichkeiten, die sie ins Dasein gerufen haben? Ohne die Männer und Frauen, die vom ersten Tag an mit ganzem Herzen und unerschütterlichem Engagement dabei waren. Sie haben Visionen geschmiedet, schwere Lasten getragen, Böden gereinigt und großzügig gespendet. Es sind jene stillen Architekten, die Großes vollbracht haben. Ohne ihren selbstlosen Einsatz gäbe es diesen Ort nicht – eine Tatsache, die jedem Besucher in ihrer vollen Tragweite bewusst sein sollte.
Sie legten den unverzichtbaren Grundstein; nachfolgende Generationen haben dieses wertvolle Erbe bewahrt und weiterentwickelt. Die heutigen wie zukünftigen Gemeindemitglieder sind es, die diesen Ort mit Leben erfüllen und seine Vitalität sichern. Ein Ort, der nicht nur aus Mauern besteht, sondern ein pulsierendes Herz besitzt, das für alle schlägt.
Ich wünsche jedem Einzelnen von ihnen nur das Allerbeste und die reichste Belohnung. Möge Allah jede ihrer guten Taten annehmen und segnen. Möge Allah all jenen, die ihre Zeit, Kraft, Arbeit und ihr Vermögen für diesen heiligen Ort geopfert haben, Erleichterung schenken, ihre Lasten mindern und ihnen die Tore zum Džennet weit öffnen.
Die IGBD Duisburg e. V. ist für mich ein Ort voller kostbarer Erinnerungen, unerschöpflicher Hoffnung und strahlendem Licht. Ein Ort, der mein Herz trägt. Ein Ort, an dem man Allah näherkommt. Und ein Ort, an dem man sich niemals allein fühlt, sondern stets geborgen und verbunden.
reviews.textTranslated:
★★★★★ – A Place That Holds My Heart
For me, the IGBD Duisburg e. V. is far more than just a mosque; it is a deeply rooted and formative part of my life story. Here I was able to grow up, perform my first prayers, internalize the faith, experience profound community, and always find solace when life's adversities challenged me.

This place is a refuge where my heart finds peace. Even upon entering, one is enveloped by a special aura: a stillness filled with deep peace and inner reflection. A warmth that emanates from the people, from the sincerely lived faith, and the palpable closeness to Allah. Here, Islam is practiced with love and authenticity – not superficially or ostentatiously, but from the heart and with genuine devotion.

What always impresses and deeply touches me is the immaculate purity of this place. The mosque's cleanliness is exceptional; everything is lovingly maintained down to the smallest detail, demonstrating the utmost care. One senses that this place is deeply honored, not only through words but through every action, entirely in keeping with the sublime teachings of our faith.

And what would this mosque be without the tireless individuals who brought it into being? Without the men and women who, from the very first day, were involved with their whole hearts and unwavering commitment. They forged visions, carried heavy burdens, cleaned floors, and donated generously. They are these quiet architects who accomplished great things. Without their selfless dedication, this place would not exist—a fact that every visitor should fully appreciate.

They laid the indispensable foundation; subsequent generations have preserved and developed this precious legacy. It is the current and future members of the community who fill this place with life and ensure its vitality. A place that is not just made of walls, but possesses a beating heart that beats for everyone. I wish each and every one of them only the very best and the richest reward. May Allah accept and bless every good deed they have done. May Allah grant relief to all those who have sacrificed their time, strength, work, and wealth for this holy place, lessen their burdens, and open wide the gates of Djennet for them.

For me, IGBD Duisburg e. V. is a place filled with precious memories, inexhaustible hope, and radiant light. A place that holds my heart. A place where one draws closer to Allah. And a place where one never feels alone, but always safe and connected.

reviews.name: Haris Borancic
reviews.text:
Die Moschee ist wunderschön gestaltet – sauber, ruhig und architektonisch beeindruckend. Sie ist ein wahrer Schmuck der Stadt und ein schöner Ort für das Gebet. Man sieht, dass man sich gut um den Raum kümmert, was auf jeden Fall lobenswert ist.

Ein großer Nachteil ist jedoch das Verhalten des jungen Imams. Statt offen und freundlich zu sein, wirkt er oft mürrisch und verschlossen. Er erlaubt den Gläubigen nicht, das „Amin“ laut auszusprechen – etwas, das seit Jahrhunderten in unserer Tradition verankert ist – und zwingt anderen seinen eigenen Gebetsstil auf, als ob alle anderen Formen falsch wären. Diese Haltung sorgt für Unbehagen und Spaltung unter den Betenden, anstatt Gemeinschaft und Geduld zu fördern.

Eine Moschee sollte ein Ort sein, an dem sich die Menschen willkommen und frei in ihrer Ausübung des Glaubens fühlen – im Rahmen des Islams, aber mit Verständnis für Unterschiede. Wir hoffen, dass sich auch in dieser Hinsicht etwas ändern wird.

Džamija je prelijepo uređena – čista, mirna i arhitektonski impresivna. Pravi je ukras grada i lijepo mjesto za ibadet. Očigledno je da se vodi briga o prostoru, i to zaslužuje svaku pohvalu.

Međutim, veliki nedostatak predstavlja ponašanje mladog imama. Umjesto da bude susretljiv i blizak džematlijama, često djeluje načomrđeno i zatvoreno. Ne dozvoljava ljudima da izgovaraju “Amin” na glas, što je stoljećima prisutno u našem narodu, i nameće svoj način klanjanja svima drugima, kao da su drugačiji pristupi pogrešni. Takav stav unosi nelagodu i razdor među vjernicima, umjesto da gradi zajedništvo i sabur.

Džamija treba biti mjesto gdje se ljudi osjećaju dobrodošlo i slobodno u svom ibadetu – u granicama islama, ali s razumijevanjem razlika. Nadamo se da će se i u tom pravcu nešto promijeniti.
reviews.textTranslated:
Die Moschee ist wunderschöne gestaltet – sauber, ruhig und architektonisch beeindruckend. Sie ist ein wahrer Schmuck der Stadt und ein schöner Ort für das Gebet. Man sieht, dass man sich gut um den Raum kümmert, was auf jeden Fall lobenswert ist.

Ein großer Nachteil ist jedoch das Verhalten des jungen Imams. Statt offen und freundlich zu sein, wirkt er oft mürrisch und verschlossen. Er erlaubt den Gläubigen nicht, das "Amin" laut auszusprechen - etwas, das seit Jahrhunderten in unserer Tradition verankert ist - und zwingt anderen seinen eigenen Gebetsstil auf, als ob alle anderen Formen falsch wären. Diese Haltung sorgt für Unbehagen und Spaltung unter den Betenden, nafter Gemeinschaft und Geduld zu fördern.

Eine Moschee sollte ein Ort sein, an dem sich die Menschen willkommen und frei in ihrer Ausübung des Glaubens fühlen – im Rahmen des Islams, aber mit Verständungs ​​für Unterschiede. Wir hoffen, dass sich auch in dieser Hinsicht etwas ändern wird.

The mosque is beautifully decorated – clean, peaceful and architecturally impressive. It is a true decoration of the city and a beautiful place for worship. It is obvious that the space is taken care of, and it deserves every praise.

However, the young imam's behavior is a major drawback. Instead of being accommodating and close to the congregation, he often seems sullen and closed. He does not allow people to say "Amen" out loud, which has been present in our people for centuries, and imposes his way of worship on everyone else, as if different approaches are wrong. Such an attitude brings discomfort and discord among believers, instead of building unity and harmony.

A mosque should be a place where people feel welcome and free to worship – within the boundaries of Islam, but with an understanding of differences. We hope that something will change in that direction as well.

reviews.text: Steht rund um die Uhr, aber die Türen sind verschlossen. Wie kann man damit umgehen? Die Temperatur ist 38 Grad, es ist um 15:30 Uhr und ich bin einfach vor der Tür!!!

reviews.name: Kushtrim Mati
reviews.text: War dort zum Freitagsgebet, sehr sauber, genug Platz und sehr gut organisiert. Besonders schön war es, dass es zwei Ausgänge gibt und sogar ein Fahrstuhl. Der Imam war auch sehr entspannt und hatte eine tolle ruhige Stimme. Wünschenswert wäre nur eine deutsche Version zum Freitagsgebete, wenn auch zumindest als QR-Code. Gerne wieder, inshallah
reviews.textTranslated: I attended Friday prayers there; it was very clean, spacious, and very well organized. It was especially nice that there were two exits and even an elevator. The Imam was also very relaxed and had a wonderfully calm voice. A German version of the Friday prayer schedule would be desirable, even if only as a QR code. I would gladly attend again, inshallah.
